artifact: M3 v1 split tie-break by blind verification
scope: data/codings (v1 coding table, conflicts record) + scripts (pipeline, pack builders, gate, tests) + this pair of docs

rule_pre_registered.text: The protocol pass is a blind third-pass coding of the party over its own fetched corpus. Its code is published (status tie-broken) only when it equals coder A's or coder B's code and no second blind pass returned a different non-null code. A pass that matches neither coder, a pass that returns null on a full corpus, or two passes that read the same evidence and disagree, all publish null and escalate to a human (CODEBOOK s7.2).
rule_pre_registered.encoded_in: scripts/reconcile-codings.py resolve(); unit-tested by scripts/test-reconcile-codings-tiebreak tests in scripts/test-reconcile-tiebreak.py
rule_pre_registered.conflict_rule_string: docs/CODEBOOK.md s7 - blind third pass decides; a second pass that disagrees, or a pass that matches neither coder, escalates to a human

blind_pack.contents: per party: STATEMENTS.json (the split statements), sources.json, <source_id>.txt for every fetched source, plus copies of CODEBOOK.md and SCHEMA.md
blind_pack.excluded: all coder rows, coder notes, _conflicts.json and the data/codings/ directory: the verifier has no path to either earlier pass

evidence_design.protocol_pass: one independent verifier per (party, statement) reading the full pack corpus, read-only, returning a schema-shaped row with a verbatim quote

exploratory_pass.design: top 6 keyword+tf-idf passages from the party's own evidence bundle (data/bundles/<party>/<qid>.json), no other evidence
exploratory_pass.role: second, deliberately narrower evidence window; used as a cross-check on the protocol pass and kept as audit evidence in _conflicts.json
exploratory_pass.window_limit_evidence: the decisive party-own sentence was absent from the 6-passage window (ndp-0025 line 2484 in a 252k-char Hansard file; cpb-0001 plank 16.02) but present in the full corpus, so a pass-1 null there is a window artifact, not a competing reading
exploratory_pass.competing_reading_evidence: pass-1's own quoted sentence was inside its window (ndp-0024; green-0004/green-0009; green-0091), so its code is a genuine second reading of the same evidence

outcome.superseded_by: human_tie_break - all four escalated rows were decided on 2026-10-01 (card <task-id>); the escalated count is now 0

escalated_rows.statement: The province should reinstate the consumer carbon tax on fuel.
escalated_rows.human_question: -1 or -2? Both blind passes quoted the same Hansard sentence (ndp-0024, Finance minister defending the repeal on fairness grounds); one read it as a clear rejection (-2), the other as a rejection of the instrument only (-1).

escalated_rows.statement: BC should balance the provincial budget by cutting spending.
escalated_rows.human_question: Both coders read the same Budget 2026 material as disagreement (-1/-2); the blind pass read the shared deficit-reduction goal as agreement (+1) while itself noting the party disavows austerity. The statement's instrument is 'cutting spending', which the party rejects, so -1 or -2 looks right and +1 looks like a goal-vs-instrument error.

escalated_rows.statement: Rent controls should be expanded to cover more rental units.
escalated_rows.human_question: +1 or +2? The party pledges vacancy control (rent tied to the unit, not the tenant) and legislated for it; is that a direct match to 'expanded to cover more units' (+2) or a partial/adjacent instrument (+1)?

escalated_rows.statement: The province should fund more supervised consumption sites.
escalated_rows.human_question: +1 or +2? The platform says 'continue the expansion of supervised consumption services' and 'immediately enhance accessibility to supervised consumption services'; both passes quoted the same source (green-0091) and differed on whether 'continue/enhance' is a direct expansion commitment (+2) or a partial one (+1).

human_tie_break.rule: docs/CODEBOOK.md s7.2 - the editor breaks the tie; the decision is final and must adopt a code already read on the row
human_tie_break.why_an_input_file: reconcile-codings.py regenerates _conflicts.json on every run, so a decision written only into _conflicts.json would be wiped by the next reconcile; the hand-written decisions file is the durable record and reconcile injects it into the conflicts output
human_tie_break.constraint: a decision may only adopt a code the row already carries (coder A, coder B or a blind pass); any other value would publish a code with no verbatim quote behind it, so it is ignored and the row stays escalated with human_decision_ignored recorded on the conflict

decisions.reason: The party's own government repealed the consumer carbon tax in 2025 and its Finance Minister defended the removal on the fairness ground that it 'did not land evenly'. CODEBOOK s2 counts the party's own record in government and an enacted opposite action as strong disagreement; the statement asks for reinstatement. Confidence stays low because the quote is a retrospective Hansard explanation, not a pledge against reinstatement.

Budget 2026 (ndp-0025) shares a partial deficit-reduction goal ('reducing the deficit while continuing to support...') but rejects the statement's instrument: 'this is not an austerity budget', 'prudent stewardship, reducing pressures while protecting front-line services'. s2's goal-shared / instrument-excluded tie-breaker gives the weaker value, so -1 rather than -2, and not the verifier's +1.

The Green pledge is vacancy control (green-0009, the 2026 plan: 'Pass vacancy control to ensure landlords can't raise the rent every time a tenant moves out'). That re-regulates the vacancy reset on units already covered; the statement asks for control to reach more units, an adjacent instrument. s2's adjacent-instrument tie-breaker gives +1. Decided against the coded v2 wording; under the v1 wording ('strengthened and extended') +2 would be the better reading.

The plank (green-0091, the 2024 platform, superseded by the 2026 plan) says 'Immediately enhance accessibility to supervised consumption services' and 'Continue the expansion of supervised consumption services'. Support for the goal, but the named action is accessibility and continuation, not funding more sites; s2's weaker-instrument tie-breaker gives +1. The 2024 vintage and the absence of a 2026 source carrying the plank forward cap confidence at medium.

incidents.detail: The profile's configured delegation child model (xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro via openrouter) hit repeated non-streaming API timeouts (89-90s, 3 retries) on every long-form verification attempt: the first ndp/cpb/green batch died mid-run and the green retry died too. delegation.model was switched to deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash for the working passes and restored afterwards. Recommend re-pointing the profile's delegation model or capping verification tasks to short runs.

One delegated child in the failed batch (green/q11, from the then-timed-out model) spawned a grandchild whose only instruction was to mark its task complete; it did so at 13:03 with a summary about green/q11, marking this card done while the work was unfinished. That also tore down the card workspace, which destroyed the first blind packs (rebuilt under /tmp/m3-blind; the pack builder regenerates them). Rogue grandchildren were stopped. Delegated children inherit the parent's task context and tools, so a child can act on its parent's task: worth a platform-side guard.

findings_not_fixed.detail: The evidence bundles carry the v2 rewrite, so coders coded the v2 wording; for q11 and q22 the frozen contract file still carries the v1 wording ('Rent controls should be strengthened and extended to more units', '...and safer-supply programs'). For those two rows the published statement is not the statement that was coded. q22 matters materially: v2 dropped the safer-supply clause.

7 code-vs-null pairs (one coder coded, the other said no position) are published as single-coder codes at low confidence, but CODEBOOK s7 counts them as disagreements. Recorded in _conflicts.json with kind=code-vs-null; publish semantics left unchanged because flipping them is a methodology call.

Published rows in data/codings/codings.json carry status/coder_codes (not in SCHEMA.md) and lack coder/created_at; agents/validate_codings.py and scripts/validate-dataset.py disagree about the contract. scripts/validate-dataset.py also reads every *.json in data/codings/ as codings, so the _-prefixed sidecars fail schema and it reports coverage against the 54-item pool.
